solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Small amount of study initially having importance

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word study

parts.note: something that is mattering has importance or significance

explanation.surface: A student picks up a little learning early on, and it turns out to count for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, superficial knowledge or a sprinkling, so a small quantity.

clue.text: Woman with record showing farm animals

parts.note: she is the pronoun standing for a woman
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman's record release seems to be about livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are woolly grazing livestock kept on farms, the plural being the same as the singular.

clue.text: Anxiety caused by arrest

definitions.meaning: fearful unease about what is to come
the seizing of a suspect by police

explanation.surface: Worry brought on by being taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has both a mental-state sense of dread and a legal sense of capturing someone.

clue.text: Amphibian gets kicked, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to be toed is to be struck with the toe, that is kicked

explanation.surface: A frog-like creature gets booted around, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is a warty, land-loving amphibian related to the frog.

clue.text: Redemption money a children's author talked of

indicators.note: talked of means the author's name is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote the Swallows and Amazons children's books

explanation.surface: A payment to buy someone's freedom that a writer for young readers mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome, author of Swallows and Amazons, is a classic British children's writer; his surname loses its final E when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the price paid to release a captive, literally buying them back.

clue.text: Songbird Greek character found on roofing material

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece found on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
thatch is straw or reed used to roof cottages

explanation.surface: A bird of song spotted with a Greek letter on a thatched roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small passerine bird that climbs tree trunks, a songbird in the broad sense.

clue.text: Politician vexed over new church stopping alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over, so above, the rest

parts.note: vexed means annoyed, that is cross

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters go inside the drink

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink brewed from malt

explanation.surface: An irritated MP finds a new church blocking his supply of booze.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossbencher sits in the House of Lords on benches set across from the party sides; 'stopping' makes the middle BENCHER, and 'over' puts the first part on top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbencher is a member of the House of Lords who sits for no party, a kind of independent politician.

clue.text: International organisation thus filling in agreement

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: filling means one piece goes into the other, as stuffing fills something

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A global body is thus brought into accord.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is not the insertion signal but letters; 'filling' is the signal, giving ISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in complete accord, so unison is agreement.

clue.text: Account for former partner of homely aspect

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
someone plain in looks has a homely appearance

explanation.surface: Justifying an ex who has rather a homely look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homely' here is the American sense of plain-looking, not cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to give an account of it, accounting for why it happened.

clue.text: Go across island, reaching Italian city

indicators.note: across means one piece spans the other, so the island sits within it

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Crossing over an island to arrive in a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the noun, your turn, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, Torino in Italian, is the capital of Piedmont in northern Italy.

clue.text: Not many, they say? That's a relief

indicators.note: they say tells us the word is what people pronounce, not what is spelt

parts.note: few means not many

explanation.surface: Only a few, it is said, and we can breathe easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is an exclamation people let out when tension or worry is over.

clue.text: Uncrystallised sugar produced by Missouri girls

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
lasses are girls, especially in Scotland and the North of England

explanation.surface: Some syrupy sweetener made by young women from Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left after sugar has been crystallised out of cane juice.

clue.text: Afflicted former nurse concealing subterfuge

indicators.note: concealing means the nurse holds the trick hidden inside

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a now-discontinued British nursing grade
a trick is a subterfuge, a deceitful ploy

explanation.surface: A troubled ex-nurse hiding some deception.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing qualification phased out in the 1990s, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken describes someone struck down by illness or trouble, which is being afflicted.

clue.text: Mission in Paris that served travellers principally

parts.note: que is French for that, and in Paris points to the French word

indicators.note: principally asks for the leading letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A mission in Paris that looked after travellers above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally' takes S and T from 'served travellers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a long search or undertaking, a mission to achieve something.

clue.text: Fruit-tree one of five arriving together with Civil Engineer

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five born at once

explanation.surface: A quintuplet turns up with an engineer to visit an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a tree bearing hard, fragrant pear-shaped fruit used for jelly.

clue.text: Room in taxi on the left

indicators.note: on the left places the taxi before the little word in, to its left

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Space inside a taxi on the left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not an insertion signal; it is the letters IN, with CAB put on its left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small room, especially a private one on a ship.

clue.text: Deadly obstruction originally hampering almost everyone

parts.note: a let is an obstruction or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: originally asks for just the opening letter of hampering
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A blockage that, from the start, held back nearly everybody, with fatal results.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal is capable of causing death, so it is deadly.

clue.text: Fashionable church feature dean primarily motivated

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a spire is the tapering tower on top of a church

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of dean

explanation.surface: A trendy steeple prompted the dean's thinking above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inspired means being stirred or moved to act, hence motivated.

clue.text: Photograph game

definitions.meaning: a quick informal photograph, a snapshot
a children's card game where matching cards are called out

explanation.surface: A picture of some sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a casual photo and a simple card game played by matching pairs.

clue.text: Danger of rising anger in political extremists

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the outer letters
extremists here means only the end letters of political
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: The threat posed by mounting fury among radicals in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suits a down entry, read from the bottom up, giving ERI; 'extremists' leaves only the outer letters of 'political'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious and immediate risk, a synonym for danger.

clue.text: Bridge-player missing beginning of banquet

indicators.note: missing beginning of means the first letter of the word for banquet is dropped

parts.note: a feast is a banquet

explanation.surface: A card player skips the start of a grand dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four seat positions at bridge, so a bridge player.

clue.text: Offender's supper finally eaten by chef

definitions.note: read as 'offender is', so the definition is offender with 's as a link

indicators.note: eaten by means the letter goes inside the chef

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of supper

explanation.surface: A criminal's evening meal is finished off by the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, the end of 'supper', which goes inside COOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is informally a criminal, someone who has offended against the law.

clue.text: Woman's husband caught in fire, perhaps

definitions.note: read as 'woman is', so the definition is woman with 's as a link

indicators.note: caught in means the husband is trapped inside the other word

parts.note: an electric or gas fire is an example of a heater

explanation.surface: A wife's partner is trapped in a blaze, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks fire as one example of a HEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a woman's given name, taken from the moorland plant.

clue.text: One-sided version of a Latin rule

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lopsided form of a rule from Latin grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Unilateral means done by or affecting only one side or party.
